# models.dynamics { #wdm.models.dynamics }

`models.dynamics`

The continuous-time model, its one-day step map, and the process-noise model.

Assembling the pieces, the state $x = (T, F, G_c, G_n, A)$ evolves as

$$
\begin{aligned}
\rho_{\text{eff}}\, \dot T &= I - E - \rho_G \dot G_c \\
\dot F &= p\, \dot T \\
\dot G_c &= \bigl(k_G \Delta C - G_c\bigr) / \tau_G \\
\dot G_n &= \bigl(k_{Na} \Delta \mathrm{Na} - G_n\bigr) / \tau_{Na} \\
\dot A &= \bigl(-\beta_A (E_{\text{base}} - I) - A\bigr) / \tau_A
\end{aligned}
$$

The term $\rho_G \dot G_c$ is easy to overlook and worth stating plainly:
energy diverted into glycogen storage is energy not available for fat storage.
Omitting it makes the model attribute the entire post-refeed scale jump to
tissue gain, which is both wrong and, if you are the one reading the output,
needlessly discouraging.

Two integrators are provided. `step` is a fixed-step RK4 map used inside
the filter, where it runs millions of times and must be fast and
trace-friendly. `simulate_diffrax` is an adaptive-step reference used for
validation. A test asserts the two agree to tight tolerance; if they ever
diverge, the fixed-step map's substep count is the first thing to raise.

### NoiseModel { #wdm.models.dynamics.NoiseModel }

```python
models.dynamics.NoiseModel()
```

Process and observation noise.

Process noise represents everything the deterministic model leaves out:
unlogged snacks, hydration swings, measurement drift in the food log,
day-to-day variation in spontaneous activity. Standard deviations are
per-day, so variance accumulates linearly with elapsed time -- which is what
makes a week-long gap in weigh-ins widen the confidence band by
$\sqrt{7}$ rather than by 7.

#### Attributes

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [unlogged_intake_sd](#wdm.models.dynamics.NoiseModel.unlogged_intake_sd) | kcal/day. Spread of plausible intake on days with no food log. |

### process_noise { #wdm.models.dynamics.process_noise }

```python
models.dynamics.process_noise(x, u, p, noise)
```

Process-noise covariance for one day, ``(5, 5)``.

Diagonal in the state variables, plus a rank-one inflation on the days with
no food log, and on days whose log is an estimate (``u.intake_sd_kcal``,
the logged energy's own uncertainty). The inflation is *not* diagonal: an
unknown intake perturbs tissue and fat mass together, in the fixed ratio set by the current
partitioning, so it enters as $\sigma_I^2 b b^\top$ with

$$
b = \frac{1}{\rho_{\text{eff}}}\,(1,\ p,\ 0,\ 0,\ 0)^\top .
$$

Getting this correlation right matters. Treating the two as independent
would let the filter believe it could learn fat mass from a day it knows
nothing about, which is precisely the sort of phantom information that makes
a filter overconfident.

### rate { #wdm.models.dynamics.rate }

```python
models.dynamics.rate(x, u, p, carb_ref_g)
```

Time derivative of the state, in units per day.

Returns a `State` whose fields are rates rather than values -- a mild
abuse of the type that keeps the arithmetic readable and costs nothing,
since both are the same pytree shape.

### simulate { #wdm.models.dynamics.simulate }

```python
models.dynamics.simulate(
    x0,
    inputs,
    p,
    carb_ref_g,
    *,
    substeps=DEFAULT_SUBSTEPS,
)
```

Roll the model forward over a whole episode.

``inputs`` is a `DailyInput` whose fields are arrays of length ``n``.
Returns a `State` whose fields are arrays of length ``n``, giving the
state *after* each day.

### simulate_diffrax { #wdm.models.dynamics.simulate_diffrax }

```python
models.dynamics.simulate_diffrax(
    x0,
    inputs,
    p,
    carb_ref_g,
    *,
    rtol=1e-08,
    atol=1e-10,
)
```

Adaptive-step reference integration, one day at a time.

Slower than `simulate` and not used inside the filter. Its purpose is
to be the trusted answer that the fast path is checked against, so that a
discretisation error can never masquerade as a physiological finding.

### step { #wdm.models.dynamics.step }

```python
models.dynamics.step(x, u, p, carb_ref_g, *, substeps=DEFAULT_SUBSTEPS)
```

Advance the state by exactly one day using fixed-step RK4.

Inputs are held constant across the day, making this an exact zero-order-hold
discretisation of the continuous model -- the correct reading of a daily food
log, which reports a total rather than an instantaneous rate.

### step_vector { #wdm.models.dynamics.step_vector }

```python
models.dynamics.step_vector(xv, u, p, carb_ref_g, *, substeps=DEFAULT_SUBSTEPS)
```

Vector-in, vector-out form of `step`, for the filters.
